paletteRules.statusInk: ramp 300 in dark, 700 in light; soft = ramp 500 at 12%

narrative.overview:
Toad is a measuring instrument that sits next to the editor: a near-colorless ground, a chrome-coloured rail and header, hairline cards, and literal values set in mono so they read like readouts. Color is rationed. One accent (Mint by default) marks what you can act on and what you have chosen; status hues mean status; chart series are the only place hue carries data. Everything else is ground, line and text in four steps.

The world is Saga's: true black in dark, warm paper in light, built at runtime from OKLCH ramps in `src/lib/theme.ts` so charts and CSS share one palette. The accent is a per-machine preference across six packs (Violet, Blue, Mint, Lime, Amber, Coral); every rule here is written against roles, not hues, so it holds for any pack. Density is desktop-tool density: 13px body, 32px controls, 12px card radii, and no decoration that isn't carrying information. The signature is the drawn load profile: the plan is a line you drag, and the same chart later lays the achieved run over it.

The system refuses the category default of one long form beside a dashboard, and it refuses decorative color: no gradients, no tinted card backgrounds, no colored rail bars.
keyCharacteristics: True-black (dark) or warm-paper (light) ground; the chrome (rail, header, footer, outline) is the same ground, divided by hairlines.
One accent, used only for the primary action, selection, focus and the planned-load line.
Instrument Sans for interface text; Geist Mono with tabular figures for every literal value, URL, method and number.
Five type sizes; hierarchy comes from weight and text tone, not more sizes.
Flat panels with hairline edges; shadow only on things that float.
Drawn, single-weight SVG icons; no glyphs standing in for icons.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The accent marks exactly four things: the primary action, selection, focus, and the planned load. A screen at rest shows it on Start and on whatever is selected, nowhere else.

rules.name: The No Side Bar Rule
rules.body: The active rail item is a full accent-wash fill with an accent-ink icon. It never carries a colored side stripe.

rules.name: The Data Never Borrows Rule
rules.body: Chart series are never the accent. Plans are the dashed accent line; achieved load over a plan is drawn in `text`; targets and reference lines are neutral `text4`, dashed.

rules.name: The Token Tone Rule
rules.body: In templates and resolved previews: variables and resolved values are info, generators are neutral raised2, pending tokens are warning, unknown or invalid tokens are danger. Secrets render as masked dots, never colored.

rules.name: The Five Sizes Rule
rules.body: Exactly five sizes (11, 12, 13, 15, 20). Hierarchy comes from weight (400/500/600) and text tone (text to text4), not from new sizes.

rules.name: The Literal Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Every literal value, URL, header, HTTP method, variable name and number is Geist Mono with tabular figures. Error rates show one decimal, or two when one decimal would hide which side of an in-scope bound the value is on. Verdict values carry their unit.

rules.name: The Only Floaters Cast Rule
rules.body: A card on the window has a hairline and no shadow. If it does not float above other content, it does not get the pop shadow.

dos: **Do** take every color from the runtime palette roles (`--bg`, `--panel`, `--line2`, `--accent-soft`); never hard-code a hex in a component, so all six accents and both themes keep working.
**Do** set every literal value, URL, method and number in Geist Mono with tabular figures, and give verdict values their unit.
**Do** mark selection with the accent wash (plus a 1px inset accent ring on list rows) and keep Start the only accent-filled button on screen.
**Do** draw plans as dashed accent, achieved-over-plan as solid `text`, and targets or references as dashed `text4`.
**Do** put round 1/2/2.5/5×10ⁿ ticks with one precision on every chart axis, and a legend on every chart with more than one line.
**Do** use the drawn SVG icon set in `ui.tsx` for every icon, including arrows used as icons.
donts: **Don't** use the accent for chart series, status, decoration, or a colored side bar on the active rail item.
**Don't** add a shadow to a card that sits on the window; shadow belongs only to floating surfaces.
**Don't** introduce a sixth type size; reach for weight or text tone instead.
**Don't** use Unicode glyphs as stand-ins for icons. Arrows inside prose and native dialog text are fine.
**Don't** let a status hue sit within 26° of the accent, or a series within 60°; the palette builder enforces this, so don't override it.
**Don't** put a small uppercase label above a heading; uppercase micro is only the heading of a list group.
